q: 面试官禁止使用 Elasticsearch / Postgres 全文索引后，设计上你被迫要亲手做的核心工作是？
q_en: When Elasticsearch and Postgres full-text search are off limits, what core work must you build yourself?
options: 亲手设计数据布局与倒排索引
改用 NoSQL 自带的搜索功能
放弃关键词搜索改做前缀匹配
把过滤逻辑全放到客户端本地
why: 没有现成全文索引可依赖，你必须自己决定数据如何布局、如何构建倒排索引、如何扩展——这正是这类题要考的底层功。
why_en: With no off-the-shelf full-text index available, you must design the data layout, build the inverted index, and scale it yourself.
options_en: Hand-build the data layout and an inverted index yourself.
Rely on a NoSQL database's built-in search.
Drop keyword search and only do prefix matching.
Push all filtering to the client side.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开箱即用的分布式搜索引擎，内部本身就用倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an off-the-shelf search engine built on inverted indexes.

optionExplanations: 禁用现成引擎后，唯一出路就是这个：自己定布局、建索引、想扩展。
误以为 NoSQL 自带全文检索能绕过限制，但题目已经排除了这类现成搜索方案。
把关键词搜索偷换成前缀匹配，其实是在悄悄阉割功能需求，题目并未允许。
客户端拿不到全量帖子数据，把过滤全丢给它做不出真正的搜索匹配。
optionExplanations_en: With Elasticsearch and native full-text search off the table, you're the one deciding the data layout, the index shape, and how it scales.
NoSQL's built-in search is exactly the kind of off-the-shelf engine this problem rules out, so it doesn't get you out of building your own.
Swapping keyword search for prefix matching quietly drops a stated requirement instead of solving the indexing problem.
The client never sees the full post corpus, so pushing filtering there can't reproduce real keyword search.
scenario: 面试官禁掉 Elasticsearch 和 Postgres 全文索引，你仍要在万亿级帖子上支持关键词搜索。
scenario_en: The interviewer takes Elasticsearch and Postgres full-text search off the table, but you still need keyword search over a trillion posts.

q: 为 FB 帖子搜索定义需求时，哪些属于核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: When defining requirements for FB Post Search, which are core functional requirements?
options: 用户能创建和点赞帖子
用户能按关键词搜索帖子
搜索结果能按时间或点赞数排序
搜索结果按用户兴趣做个性化排序
why: 核心需求只有三条：创建/点赞、关键词搜索、按时间或赞数排序；个性化被明确划出范围，这个决定让后面的缓存设计大为简化。
why_en: The core requirements are creating and liking posts, keyword search, and sorting by recency or like count, while personalization is explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Users can create and like posts.
Users can search posts by keyword.
Results can be sorted by recency or like count.
Results are personalized to each user's interests.
optionExplanations: 创建和点赞是搜索得以运作的前提动作，属于核心功能需求。
关键词搜索是本题唯一被点名的核心检索方式，必须支持。
结果排序是明确列出的核心需求，为后面的双索引设计埋下伏笔。
个性化听起来像加分项，但被题目明确划出范围，不是核心需求。
optionExplanations_en: Creating and liking posts are the baseline actions the whole search feature depends on, so they're core requirements.
Keyword search is the one retrieval mode this problem names explicitly, so it has to be supported.
Sorting results is called out as a core requirement, which is what later motivates the dual-index design.
Personalization sounds like a nice add-on, but the problem explicitly puts it out of scope, not a core requirement.
scenario: 为 FB 帖子搜索划需求：10 亿用户 × 每天 1 帖 ≈ 10k 帖/秒，40 分钟白板只能设计最小可用集。
scenario_en: Scoping FB Post Search: 1B users times one post a day is roughly 10K posts per second, and on a 40-minute whiteboard you can only design the minimum viable set.

q: FB 帖子搜索里，下列哪些被划为范围外（out of scope）？（多选）
q_en: In FB Post Search, which items are out of scope?
options: 模糊匹配（搜 bird 命中 ostrich）
隐私规则与过滤
新帖 1 分钟内可被搜索
搜索页对新帖做实时推送更新
why: 模糊匹配、个性化、隐私、复杂相关性排序、多媒体、实时更新都在范围外；「新帖 1 分钟内可搜」恰恰是核心非功能需求，不是范围外。
why_en: Fuzzy matching, privacy filters, and realtime result updates are out of scope, whereas making new posts searchable within a minute is a core requirement.
options_en: Fuzzy matching (searching bird also matches ostrich).
Privacy rules and filtering.
New posts searchable within one minute.
Realtime push updates to the search page.
optionExplanations: 模糊匹配要理解语义相近词，这类高级检索能力被划出了范围。
隐私规则涉及权限体系，这道题聚焦索引和检索，不含在内。
这条其实是核心非功能需求（新帖可搜的时限），不是范围外项目。
实时推送要额外的长连接和通知系统，本题只做拉取式搜索。
optionExplanations_en: Fuzzy matching needs semantic-similarity understanding, an advanced capability this problem puts out of scope.
Privacy rules are an authorization concern; this problem stays focused on indexing and retrieval, not access control.
This is actually a core non-functional requirement — the new-post visibility deadline — not an out-of-scope item.
Realtime push needs long-lived connections and a notification system; this design only does pull-based search.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索定范围：万亿帖、40 分钟白板，多留一项能力就要挤掉索引设计的时间。
scenario_en: Scoping FB Post Search over a trillion posts on a 40-minute whiteboard — every extra capability you keep eats into index-design time.

scenario: 需求阶段决定是否保留「搜索结果个性化」：10 亿用户 × 每天 1 次搜索 ≈ 10k 查询/秒，且重复查询极多。
scenario_en: During requirements you decide whether personalized results stay in scope: 1B users times one search a day is about 10K queries per second, and the same queries repeat constantly.
q: 把个性化划出范围，对系统设计最大的红利是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest system-design benefit of making personalization out of scope?
options: 数据库可以少建一个索引来省空间
读写请求都不再需要 API 网关拦截
相同查询人人同结果，查询级缓存极其有效
写入路径可以完全省掉
why: 没有个性化意味着搜索结果只取决于查询本身、人人相同，结果可以进缓存和 CDN 被海量复用；所以值得当面问「个性化是不是硬需求」。
why_en: Dropping personalization means identical queries return identical results for everyone, which makes query-level caching and CDN reuse dramatically more effective.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品硬性要求千人千面的搜索结果，查询级缓存基本失效，只能退到缓存更底层的索引数据、在线上做个性化重排。
options_en: The database needs one fewer index.
You no longer need an API gateway.
Identical queries return identical results, so query-level caching becomes extremely effective.
The write path can be dropped entirely.
tradeoff: 无个性化换来缓存高复用 vs 千人千面的相关性

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径最前端的入口，负责鉴权、限流后转发给后端服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway authenticates and rate-limits requests before forwarding them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

optionExplanations: 少建索引只是锦上添花的小事，撑不起「舍弃个性化」这么大的取舍。
API 网关管的是鉴权限流，跟结果是否因人而异毫无关系。
无个性化时同一查询谁来查结果都一样，缓存可以被海量请求复用，这才是真正的红利。
发帖点赞的写入路径跟个性化无关，砍掉个性化也不会让写入消失。
optionExplanations_en: Trimming one database index is a footnote, not the payoff big enough to justify dropping personalization.
The API gateway just handles auth and rate limiting, unrelated to whether results differ per user.
Without personalization, identical queries return identical results for everyone, so a shared cache absorbs massive request volume — that's the real win.
The write path for posts and likes has nothing to do with personalization; dropping it doesn't remove writes.

scenario: FB Post Search 面试先给定两个目标：中位搜索延迟 <500ms，新帖 <1分钟可搜。这些是 SLO/SLA 目标，不是由帖子量公式算出的结果。
scenario_en: In the FB Post Search interview, median search latency under 500 ms and new posts searchable within one minute are given SLO/SLA targets, not capacity-derived numbers.
q: 这些 NFR 数字分别约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Which design paths do these NFR numbers constrain?
text: 500ms 约束{{查询路径}}，推动内存索引、缓存和避免请求时全量排序；1分钟约束{{新帖可见性}}，反推索引流水线延迟和缓存 TTL 上限。
why: 这两个数不是算出来的容量结果，而是面试中先约定的用户体验目标。真正的计算发生在后面：用它们倒推索引、缓存、冷热分层和写入流水线。
why_en: The five-hundred-millisecond and one-minute numbers are service targets, not derived constants, and they constrain the query path and freshness path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟、吞吐、可用性这类衡量系统「好不好」的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover latency, throughput, and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队希望系统达到的内部目标，如中位搜索 <500ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level objective is an internal target for system behavior, such as median search latency under five hundred milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议：对外承诺的服务指标，如新帖 1 分钟内可搜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level agreement is a promised service level, such as new posts being searchable within a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存存活时间。超过 TTL 后缓存条目过期，系统必须重新取或重算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time to live is how long a cache entry may live before it expires and must be refreshed.

q: 「老帖、冷门帖也要可搜索，但允许更慢」这条需求在为哪个设计决策埋伏笔？
q_en: Which later design decision is hinted by the requirement that old and unpopular posts are searchable but slower?
options: 放弃高可用目标
冷热分层：热数据进内存、冷数据下沉廉价存储
换一台内存更大的单机数据库来扛全部数据
把所有索引都搬进 CDN
why: 大数据量系统天然有热/冷数据之分：热数据高频访问要内存级速度，冷数据低频访问可放磁盘、远端库甚至磁带；这条 NFR 正是后面「冷索引下沉 S3」的伏笔。
why_en: Allowing old or unpopular posts to be slower foreshadows a hot-cold split where hot data lives in memory and cold data moves to cheaper, slower storage.
options_en: Abandon the high-availability goal.
A hot-cold split: hot data in memory, cold data on cheaper storage.
Switch to a single bigger database machine.
Move all indexes into the CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: 允许冷帖慢一点跟放弃高可用是两码事，系统仍要保持可用。
这正是后面冷索引下沉 blob 存储的伏笔：热数据留内存，冷数据可以慢。
单机再大也扛不住海量冷热数据，纵向扩容不是长久之计。
CDN 缓存的是响应结果，不是拿来放整份可写索引的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Tolerating slower cold posts is not the same as giving up on availability; the system still has to stay up.
This is exactly what later motivates demoting cold indexes to blob storage: hot data stays in memory, cold data can be slower.
No single machine, however large, absorbs unbounded hot-and-cold data growth; vertical scaling doesn't hold up.
A CDN caches response payloads, not a place to host a live, writable index.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索里绝大多数查询命中近期热帖，但万亿老帖也要能搜到，全放内存的成本不可接受。
scenario_en: In FB Post Search almost every query hits recent hot posts, yet a trillion old posts must stay searchable and keeping them all in memory is unaffordable.

q: 补全写入侧的规模估算（10 亿用户，每天按约 10 万秒取整）：
q_en: Fill in the write-side scale estimate for 1B users and roughly 100K seconds per day.
text: 每人每天 1 帖 → 约 {{10k}} posts/秒；每人每天 10 个赞 → 约 {{100k}} likes/秒；点赞写入量是发帖的 {{10}} 倍。
why: 用 1B ÷ 100k 秒的快捷除法得出发帖 10k/s、点赞 100k/s；点赞比发帖多一个数量级，这个观察直接决定了后面必须重点优化点赞写入。
why_en: A billion users produce roughly ten thousand posts and one hundred thousand likes per second, so likes outnumber post creations ten to one.
scenario: 规模估算：10 亿用户，每天约 10 万秒，估算写入侧的量级。
scenario_en: Estimate write-side order of magnitude from 1B users and about 100K seconds per day.

q: 由这个读规模，读路径最该具备的能力是？
q_en: Given this read scale, what capability does the read path need most?
options: 读会突发到 10 倍，重复查询要能被缓存/CDN 吸收
读量极小，单台普通机器就足以稳稳承载全部流量
读远大于写，应把机器全都堆到读路径上、给倒排索引不断扩容
读流量根本无法估算，直接跳过这步
why: 搜索读约 10k/s 但可能突发 10 倍；因为无个性化、查询重复度高，读路径靠结果缓存和 CDN 吸收峰值，而不是一味加索引机器。
why_en: Search reads run about ten thousand per second but can spike tenfold, so the read path leans on result caching and a CDN to absorb bursts.
scenario: 10 亿用户 × 每人每天约 1 次搜索 ≈ 10k 查询/秒，还可能突发到平时的 10 倍。
scenario_en: A billion users times about one search a day is roughly 10K queries per second, and it can burst to ten times that.
options_en: Reads can spike 10x, so repeated queries must be absorbable by a cache/CDN.
Read volume is tiny; a single machine can carry all traffic.
Reads dominate writes, so pile machines onto the read path and keep scaling up the inverted index.
Read traffic can't be estimated, so skip this step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

optionExplanations: 10k/s 的常态读量还可能突发到 10 倍，读路径得靠缓存和 CDN 顶住峰值。
1 万/秒已经不是单机量级，读量并不小。
前面已经算出写才是大头，这里反而说读碾压写，判断反了。
估算恰恰是这一步的意义所在，「无法估算」是在回避该做的工作。
optionExplanations_en: A steady ten thousand reads a second can still burst tenfold, so the read path leans on cache and CDN to absorb spikes.
Ten thousand requests a second is well past what a single box handles; the volume isn't tiny.
The earlier estimate already showed writes dominate; claiming reads crush writes gets the comparison backwards.
Estimating scale is the whole point of this step; skipping it dodges the work instead of doing it.

q: 对比估算结果（写约 110k/s vs 搜索 10k/s），关于系统性质最重要的结论是？
q_en: Comparing about 110K writes/s with 10K searches/s, what is the key system takeaway?
options: 系统读多写少，应重点优化读路径、把大部分机器投在查询侧
系统写多读少——别被「搜索」二字骗成读为主
读写均衡，无需特别优化
数据量不大，单机即可承载
why: 这题最容易犯的错是被「搜索系统」带偏、假设读是大头；估算揭示写入（尤其点赞）远超读，写路径才是主要瓶颈。
why_en: The estimates reveal a write-heavy system, overturning the common assumption that a search problem must be read-heavy.
options_en: The system is read-heavy, so focus optimization on the read path and put most machines on the query side.
The system is write-heavy—don't let the word 'search' fool you into assuming reads dominate.
Reads and writes are balanced; no special optimization.
The data is small; one machine suffices.
optionExplanations: 这正是「搜索」二字带来的常见误判，估算结果其实相反。
110k/s 写 vs 10k/s 读，写才是十倍量级的大头。
两者相差一个数量级，说「均衡」低估了真实的写入压力。
十亿用户规模下的写入量早已远超单机承载能力。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the misread the word 'search' invites; the estimate actually points the other way.
At roughly 110K writes/s versus 10K reads/s, writes outweigh reads by a full order of magnitude.
The two differ by 10x, so calling it 'balanced' understates the real write pressure.
At a billion-user scale, write volume already far exceeds what one machine can carry.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索：10 亿用户每天发 1 帖、点 10 个赞、搜 1 次，你要决定先优化哪条路径。
scenario_en: FB Post Search: a billion users each post once, like ten times, and search once a day — you decide which path to optimize first.

q: 这个存储量级对搜索系统提出的设计要求是？
q_en: What does this storage scale force the search system to do?
options: 内存放不下 3.6PB，索引要设上限、冷数据下沉便宜存储
数据量不大，一台大内存机器即可
把全部帖子原文连同索引都整份塞进 Redis 内存里加速查询
存储不是问题，无需特别处理
why: 3.6 万亿帖 × 1kb ≈ 3.6PB，全量放内存/单机不可行；这直接催生后面给索引设上限、把冷门关键词下沉 blob 存储的设计。
why_en: Ten years of a billion posts a day is about 3.6 petabytes, far too much to keep in memory, which forces index caps and cold blob storage.
scenario: FB 运营 10 年、每天约 10 亿帖、每帖元数据约 1kb，原始存储估算约 3.6 PB。
scenario_en: After 10 years at roughly 1B posts per day and 1 KB metadata per post, raw storage is about 3.6 PB.
options_en: 3.6 PB won't fit in memory, so indexes must be capped and cold data pushed to cheap storage.
The data is small; one big-memory machine is enough.
Stuff every post's full text and index into Redis memory to speed up queries.
Storage isn't a concern; no special handling needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

optionExplanations: 3.6PB 远超任何单机内存容量，索引必须设上限、冷数据另找便宜去处。
3.6PB 早已超出「一台大内存机器」能装下的范围。
把原文塞进内存型的 Redis，成本和容量都撑不住 PB 级数据。
3.6PB 正是逼出「索引设上限+冷数据下沉」设计的根源，不能忽视。
optionExplanations_en: 3.6 petabytes dwarfs any single machine's memory, so indexes need a cap and cold data needs a cheaper home.
3.6 petabytes is already far beyond what one big-memory box can hold.
Stuffing raw post text into memory-priced Redis can't afford petabyte-scale cost or capacity.
3.6 petabytes is precisely what forces the index-cap-plus-cold-storage design; it can't be waved away.

q: FB 帖子搜索的核心实体（User/Post/Like）里，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about the core User/Post/Like entities in FB Post Search are correct?
options: User——发帖的主体
Post——被搜索的对象，有内容、作者，隐含点赞数
Like——我们主要关心它的计数而非每条记录
Comment——搜索的主要目标
why: 实体刻意简单：User、Post、Like 三个，且对 Like 只关心 count；实体简单就不必恋战，快速推进到 API 和设计。
why_en: The entities are just User, Post, and Like, and for likes we mostly care about the count rather than individual records.
options_en: User — the author who creates posts.
Post — the searchable object with content, author, and an implicit like count.
Like — we mostly care about its count, not each record.
Comment — the primary search target.
optionExplanations: User 只是发帖的主体，本题不深挖用户模型本身。
Post 是搜索真正的目标对象，携带内容、作者和点赞数。
点赞我们只关心总数用于排序，单条点赞记录不重要。
评论从未出现在本题的核心实体里，搜索的目标始终是帖子。
optionExplanations_en: User is just the actor who creates posts; this problem doesn't dig into the user model itself.
Post is the actual object being searched, carrying content, author, and an implicit like count.
For likes we only care about the running total for sorting, not each individual like record.
Comments never appear among this problem's core entities; the search target is always the post.
scenario: FB 帖子搜索白板只有 40 分钟，核心实体这一步该压到 2 分钟，多写实体就少了深挖时间。
scenario_en: You have 40 minutes on the FB Post Search whiteboard; core entities should take two of them, and extra entities cost you deep-dive time.

q: FB 帖子搜索的 API 应该是什么形状？
q_en: What shape should the FB Post Search API have?
options: 单一搜索端点，写入直连数据库

why_en: The system exposes a write path for posts and likes plus a search query path, and in production the writes would likely arrive via an event stream like Kafka.
options_en: A single search endpoint, with writes going straight to the database.
Everything collapsed into one GraphQL endpoint.
Search just reuses the write endpoint, sharing one API path for reads and writes.
A write path (create post / like) plus a query path (search) — two legs.

q: 设计只聚焦「搜索」时，对上游 Post Service / Like Service 的正确处理方式是？
q_en: If the design focuses only on search, how should you treat upstream Post and Like services?
options: 假设它们已存在且正常工作，只从它们接收事件
必须从零开始重新设计发帖和点赞这两个上游服务
把它们合并进搜索服务统一实现
忽略它们，让客户端直连索引
why: 搜索只是整个社交产品的一部分，合理做法是假设上游发帖/点赞服务存在并工作正常，我们的摄取层从它们接事件；把边界说清楚能省下宝贵时间。
why_en: Since we are only designing search, we assume the upstream post and like services already exist and feed our ingestion pipeline.
options_en: Assume they already exist and work; just consume their events.
Design both the post and like upstream services from scratch.
Merge them into the search service.
Ignore them and let clients hit the index directly.
optionExplanations: 搜索只是整个产品的一部分，划清边界后专心做摄取和索引。
重新设计发帖/点赞服务偏离了「只做搜索」的题目边界。
合并服务混淆了职责边界，搜索不该兼管发帖点赞的业务逻辑。
跳过上游服务，索引就没有数据来源，搜索无从谈起。
optionExplanations_en: Search is only one slice of the product, so drawing that boundary lets you focus on ingestion and indexing.
Redesigning the post and like services strays outside the 'search only' scope this problem sets.
Merging the services blurs ownership; search shouldn't also own posting and liking business logic.
Skip the upstream services and the index has no data source at all — there's nothing left to search.
scenario: 你只负责 Facebook 的搜索子系统，发帖和点赞由别的团队的服务拥有，40 分钟不够重画整个社交产品。
scenario_en: You own only Facebook's search subsystem; posting and liking belong to other teams' services, and 40 minutes isn't enough to redraw the whole product.

q: 用这条 SQL 直接在 PB 级帖子表上做关键词搜索，最根本的问题是？
q_en: What is the fundamental problem with running this SQL keyword search directly on a PB-scale posts table?
options: 语法不合法，无法执行
没有索引，查询时要逐帖全表扫描，PB 级下太慢
返回的结果不正确
LIKE 这条语法本身并不支持中文内容匹配
why: 前置通配符的 LIKE 无法走索引，每次查询都要在查询时刻扫描每一帖；结果正确但在万亿帖、PB 级数据上是灾难——数据组织必须匹配请求模式。
why_en: A leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use an index, so every query scans every post at query time, which is hopeless at petabyte scale.
options_en: The syntax is invalid and won't run.
No index is usable, so every query scans all posts — hopeless at petabyte scale.
The returned results are incorrect.
LIKE doesn't support non-English text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

optionExplanations: 这条 SQL 语法完全合法，能正常执行，只是慢到不可用。
前置通配符的 LIKE 走不了索引，每次查询都要扫全表。
结果本身是对的，问题出在扫描代价，不是结果错误。
LIKE 对语言无感知，真正的病根是缺索引而非语言支持。
optionExplanations_en: The SQL syntax is perfectly valid and runs fine; the problem is that it's unusably slow.
A leading-wildcard LIKE can't use an index, so every query scans the entire table.
The results themselves are correct; the issue is scan cost, not wrong output.
LIKE has no awareness of language at all; the real defect is the missing index, not text support.
scenario: 在万亿行、PB 级的 posts 表上直接用 LIKE '%keyword%' 查询，中位延迟目标 500ms。
scenario_en: Running LIKE '%keyword%' straight against a petabyte-scale posts table of a trillion rows, with a 500ms median latency target.

q: 对全表扫描方案做分片/复制（M 个节点各扫 N/M 帖），结论是？
q_en: If you shard and replicate the full-table scan across M nodes, what is the conclusion?
options: 分片能彻底解决扫描慢的问题
只要把节点数 M 撑到足够大，每片扫描量小到就能达标
只是边际改善：每节点仍要扫海量，依旧太慢，死路
分片反而会让结果不正确
why: 分片把扫描量从 N 降到 N/M，但面对万亿级帖子这只是把「不可能」变成「依然不可能」；正确出路是改变数据组织方式，而不是堆机器硬扫。
why_en: Sharding the naive scan only cuts each node's work to N over M posts, which is still far too slow and a dead end.
options_en: Sharding fully solves the slow-scan problem.
It's fine as long as node count M is large enough that each shard's scan is tiny.
Only a marginal gain: each node still scans a huge amount — still too slow, a dead end.
Sharding makes the results incorrect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

optionExplanations: 分片只是把慢均摊到多台机器，扫描这件事本身没有变快。
把 M 堆得再大，万亿级数据下每片仍是海量，撑不起亚秒级。
分片只把总扫描量摊薄成 N/M，量级依旧巨大，唯一出路是重新组织数据。
分片只影响谁去扫，不影响扫描逻辑本身，结果依旧正确。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding just spreads the slowness across machines; scanning itself doesn't get any faster.
However large M gets, each shard of a trillion-row table is still huge and can't hit sub-second latency.
Cutting N down to N/M only turns 'impossible' into 'still impossible' — the fix has to be reorganizing the data itself.
Sharding only changes who does the scanning, not the scan logic, so results stay correct.
scenario: 万亿帖全表扫描太慢，有人提议扩到 1000 个节点各扫 N/M 帖，延迟仍要压在 500ms 内。
scenario_en: Full scans over a trillion posts are too slow, so someone proposes a thousand nodes each scanning N/M posts — still inside a 500ms budget.

scenario: 万亿级帖子，要求按关键词找出所有包含该词的帖子，查询延迟中位数 <500ms，且不允许使用现成搜索引擎。
scenario_en: Across trillions of posts, you need sub-500 ms keyword lookup without using an off-the-shelf search engine.
q: 应该采用的核心数据结构是？
q_en: What core data structure should you use?
options: 倒排索引：关键词 → 包含它的帖子 ID 列表
对 content 列建 B-tree 索引
分片后的并行全表扫描
用布隆过滤器直接返回结果
why: 倒排索引把工作移到写入时：发帖时拆词并把帖子 ID 挂到每个词的列表下，查询就变成一次按 key 取列表的快速查找，这是关键词搜索的教科书解法。
why_en: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of posts containing it, turning search into a fast key lookup instead of a scan.
whenOtherWins: 若查询是前缀或范围查询，B-tree 类索引才有用武之地；若允许用 Elasticsearch，直接用它内置的倒排索引省去自建成本。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["新帖: I saw Taylor"] --> T["拆词 tokenization"]
    T --> A["key: i ← post9"]
    T --> B["key: saw ← post9"]
    T --> C["key: taylor ← post9"]
    Q["搜索 taylor"] -. 直接取列表 .-> C
options_en: An inverted index: keyword → list of post IDs containing it.
A B-tree index on the content column.
Parallel full-table scan after sharding.
Use a Bloom filter to return results directly.
tradeoff: 写时预组织(倒排索引) vs 查询时扫描/过滤

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库常用的按值排序索引，擅长前缀和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index sorts values for fast prefix and range lookups.

optionExplanations: 把词到帖子的映射提前建在写入阶段，检索时只是一次哈希查找，天然扛得住亚秒级要求。
B-tree 擅长前缀和范围查询，但整词精确匹配靠它仍要扫描，帮不上这里的忙。
并行扫描把 N 降到 N/M，可万亿级数据下每片仍太大，赶不上 500ms。

A B-tree shines at prefix and range lookups, but exact whole-word matching still forces a scan, so it doesn't help here.
Parallel scanning cuts N down to N/M, but each shard of a trillion posts is still too large to hit 500ms.
A Bloom filter can only answer 'maybe present,' not hand back the actual list of matching posts search needs.

q: 补全倒排索引的写入流程：
q_en: Fill in the write flow for building an inverted index:
text: 帖子创建后，Ingestion 服务把内容拆解成一个个可匹配的关键词，这个过程叫 {{tokenization}}；随后把该帖的 {{post ID}} 追加到每个关键词对应的列表里。
why: 倒排索引的构建就是「拆词 + 挂 ID」：一帖可能含 10-1000 个词，意味着一次发帖触发多个 key 的写入，这也是后面写扩展问题的根源。
why_en: Ingestion tokenizes each post into keywords and appends the post ID to every keyword's list in the index.

graph LR
    Post[New post] --> Tokenize[Tokenize text]
    Tokenize --> Terms[Terms]
    Terms --> Index[Update inverted index]
    Index --> Redis[(Redis lists or sets)]
    Post --> Store[(Post store)]

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization breaks a post into individual searchable keywords.

scenario: 倒排索引位于中位 <500ms 的核心查询路径上，需要极快的读取，同时你接受用替代方案弥补持久性短板。
scenario_en: The inverted index sits on the sub-500 ms query path, needs very fast reads, and can address durability through another option.
q: 这个倒排索引应该放在什么存储里？
q_en: Where should this inverted index live?
options: 磁盘上的 MySQL 表——最耐久但随机读取偏慢、难达亚 500ms
本地文件——最简单但单机无法扩展
Redis 内存——查询极快，MemoryDB 补持久
S3 对象存储——最便宜但延迟太高
why: 索引放 Redis 内存里查询飞快，满足亚 500ms 的核心诉求；内存的持久性短板是可解的——换 MemoryDB 等持久化兼容方案或留到深挖处理。
why_en: The index lives in Redis for blazing-fast in-memory lookups, with durability concerns addressed by a persistent alternative like MemoryDB.
whenOtherWins: 若索引重建代价不可接受、持久性是硬约束，一开始就选 MemoryDB 或磁盘型存储；冷门关键词后面也会下沉到便宜的 blob 存储。
options_en: A MySQL table on disk — most durable but random reads are too slow for sub-500ms.
Local files — simplest but a single box that can't scale.
Redis in memory — blazing-fast reads, with MemoryDB covering durability.
S3 object storage — cheapest but latency is too high.
tradeoff: 内存读取速度 vs 持久性/成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 兼容 Redis 接口但带持久化的内存数据库，可弥补纯内存的易失性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MemoryDB is a durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: MySQL 落盘最耐久，但磁盘读取撑不住亚 500ms 的核心查询路径。
本地文件简单直接，可惜是单机存储，没法随索引规模水平扩展。
内存读取满足亚 500ms 的核心诉求，持久性短板换成 MemoryDB 之类方案来补。
S3 便宜、容量大，但延迟太高，只适合放冷门数据而非热查询路径。
optionExplanations_en: MySQL on disk is the most durable option, but disk reads can't keep up with the sub-500ms query path.
Local files are simple, but they live on one box and can't scale horizontally as the index grows.
In-memory reads meet the sub-500ms requirement, and a durable variant like MemoryDB covers the persistence gap.
S3 is cheap and huge, but its latency is too high for the hot query path — better suited to cold data.

q: Redis 倒排索引方案从第一天起就自带哪些挑战？（多选）
q_en: Which challenges come with a Redis inverted-index design from day one?
options: 常见关键词的 post ID 列表会变得非常大
一帖含 10-1000 个关键词，每次发帖要写很多个 key
Redis 完全无法水平扩展
内存存储天生有持久性顾虑
why: 三大隐患：热词列表巨大（后面用截断+冷存储解决）、发帖写放大（用 Kafka+分片解决）、内存持久性（用 MemoryDB 解决）；Redis 本身完全可以通过分片水平扩展。
why_en: Common keywords produce huge ID lists, each post fans out into many key writes, and in-memory storage raises durability concerns.
options_en: Post-ID lists for common keywords grow very large.
A post has 10-1000 keywords, so each post writes many keys.
Redis can't scale horizontally at all.
In-memory storage inherently raises durability concerns.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写在底层被放大成多次物理写。

In-memory storage can lose the index on a crash, so it needs a durable fallback.

q: 把「选择倒排索引」的完整决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full decision chain for choosing an inverted index in the correct order:
steps: 代价：每帖拆出几十上百个词、每个词都要写 key；热词的 postId 列表巨大
需求：万亿帖中按关键词亚秒级找到所有匹配帖子
缓解写放大：Kafka 缓冲写入 + 索引按关键词分片
决定性质：查询时全量扫描必死，必须在写入时按查询模式预组织数据

缓解大列表：截断到 1k-10k 条 + 冷词下沉 blob 存储
why: 完整链条 = 需求 → 决定性质（写时预组织）→ 选型（Redis 倒排索引）→ 代价（写放大、大列表）→ 两条缓解各自对应一个代价；两个缓解之间先说哪个都成立。
why_en: The chain runs from the sub-second keyword search requirement, through organizing data at write time, to a Redis inverted index whose write amplification and huge lists are mitigated by buffering, sharding, capping, and cold storage.

graph TD
    Scan[Full table scan too slow] --> Inverted[Use inverted index]
    Inverted --> Redis[Fast posting lists]
    Redis --> Challenges[Memory and ranking challenges]
    Challenges --> Tiering[Hot Redis plus cold storage]
tradeoff: 写时预组织 vs 查询时扫描

q: 「请求时排序」（取出关键词全部 postId → 逐个查时间戳 → 内存排序）有哪些致命问题？（多选）

每个 postId 都要一次查找，累计上千万次查询
请求时排序百万级条目，平添不必要的延迟
排序结果一定是错误的

Each post ID needs a lookup — tens of millions of them.
Sorting millions of items at request time adds needless latency.
The sorted result is guaranteed to be wrong.

上千万次逐条查找的延迟叠加起来，远超 500ms 的预算。
把百万条目的排序留到请求时做，等于每次查询都白白多花时间。
排序算法本身没有错，问题全在代价高昂，不在结果对不对。

Head versus tail insertion is just direction — neither solves ordering by a changing score.
A single string key can't hold a ranked structure at all.
A sorted set re-orders on every like, making it the natural fit for ranking by like count.

q: 双索引方案下，发帖和点赞分别触发什么索引操作？
q_en: In the dual-index design, what index operations do posts and likes trigger?
options: 发帖只写 creation；点赞只新增 likes 条目
发帖和点赞都触发全量重建索引
发帖写两份索引(每词)；点赞更新 likes 的 score
发帖和点赞都只修改 likes index
why: 新帖要在它的每个关键词下同时进两份索引（时间序列表 + 赞数 sorted set）；点赞只需给 likes index 对应 score 加一，但高频点赞会带来巨大更新压力。
why_en: A new post is added to both indexes for every keyword it contains, while each like updates the post's score in the likes index.
options_en: A post writes only creation; a like just adds a likes entry.
Both a post and a like trigger a full index rebuild.
A post writes both indexes (per keyword); a like updates that post's score in likes.
Both posts and likes only modify the likes index.

q: 双索引方案的两个代价是？
q_en: What are the two costs of the dual-index design?
options: 存储翻倍 + 高频点赞带来海量 score 更新
查询延迟会明显变慢，且返回给用户的结果还可能不正确
索引无法分片也无法缓存
只支持英文并有内存泄漏
why: 每个关键词存两份索引，存储直接翻倍——为查询性能付的合理学费；更麻烦的是 100k/s 的点赞每个都要更新多个 sorted set，写压力成为必须解决的深挖点。
why_en: The dual indexes double storage and, worse, the heavy stream of likes forces constant score updates that stress the system.
options_en: Storage doubles, and heavy likes cause a flood of score updates.
Queries get noticeably slower and the results returned to users become incorrect.
The index can neither be sharded nor cached.
It only supports English and leaks memory.

Language support and memory leaks have nothing to do with this design choice.

scenario: 无个性化时同一查询人人同结果，新帖可见 SLA 1 分钟；10 亿用户 × 每天 1 次搜索 ≈ 10k 读/秒，可突发 10 倍。

q: 应对读流量的第一个显而易见的工具是？
q_en: What is the first obvious tool for handling read traffic?

升级更大内存的 Redis 机器
限流拒绝超额请求
结果缓存：先查缓存，未命中再搜索并回填

Upgrade to a Redis box with more memory.
Rate-limit and reject excess requests.
Result cache: check the cache first, only search and backfill on a miss.

q: 搜索结果缓存的 TTL 应该设为多少，为什么？

24 小时——尽量拉长缓存寿命把命中率做到最高

CDN edge cache: geographically local nodes cache the /search response.

Set Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600.
Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=59.
Set Expires: never.

termDefinitions.meaning: 兼容 Redis 接口但带持久化的内存数据库，可弥补纯内存的易失性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MemoryDB is a durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database.

optionExplanations: 内存本质易失，节点宕机时数据同样会丢，不只是变慢。
纯内存的唯一副本一旦宕机就可能整体丢失，得靠 MemoryDB 之类持久化方案兜底。
宕机丢的是整份索引，新旧帖子一样受影响。
CDN 只缓存 HTTP 响应，不负责恢复后端的索引数据。
optionExplanations_en: Memory is inherently volatile; a node crash loses data too, not just slows queries.
A single in-memory copy can vanish entirely on a crash, so a durable option like MemoryDB has to back it up.
A crash wipes the whole index, affecting old and new posts alike, not just new ones.
A CDN only caches HTTP responses; it has no role in restoring the backend index.
scenario: 唯一一份倒排索引放在纯内存 Redis 里，重建万亿帖索引要几天，而 NFR 要求高可用。
scenario_en: The only copy of the inverted index lives in pure in-memory Redis, rebuilding a trillion-post index takes days, and the SLA demands high availability.

q: 交集之后为什么还要「拉原文验证短语」这一步？
q_en: After intersection, why must you fetch the original text and verify the phrase?
options: 因为交集算法本身在求交过程中存在精度损失
为了顺便统计点赞数
两词都含≠短语连续，须回原文过滤假阳性
为了给缓存预热
why: 单词级索引只知道「词出现过」，不知道相邻关系；短语语义要求连续出现，必须回原文核验，否则会返回风马牛不相及的结果。
why_en: Posts containing both words separately, like Taylor made a swift exit, are false positives that only a phrase check against the original text can filter out.
options_en: Because the intersection algorithm itself loses precision while intersecting.
To count likes along the way.
Both words present does not mean a contiguous phrase, so re-check the text to filter false positives.
To warm up the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 看似匹配、实则不满足条件的结果，这里指含两词但非连续短语。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive looks like a match but is not one, e.g. both words present but not adjacent.

optionExplanations: 交集运算本身精确无误，问题出在「含两词」不等于「短语连续」。
验证短语跟统计点赞数是两套完全不相关的逻辑。
单词级索引只知道词出现过，不知道相邻关系，必须回原文核验连续性。
验证短语发生在查询路径，跟缓存预热不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: The intersection itself is exact; the gap is that containing both words isn't the same as a contiguous phrase.
Verifying a phrase and counting likes are two completely unrelated pieces of logic.
A word-level index only knows a term appeared, not adjacency, so you must re-check the original text for contiguity.
Phrase verification happens on the query path, unrelated to warming any cache.
scenario: 搜 "Taylor Swift" 时对两个单词索引求交，候选帖里这两个词可能相隔十几个字。
scenario_en: Searching "Taylor Swift" intersects two single-word indexes, and in the candidates those two words may sit a dozen words apart.

q: batcher 与里程碑更新在「对哪类帖子有效」这个维度上的区别是？
q_en: How do batcher and milestone updates differ on which posts they help?
options: 两者其实都只对少数几个高密度的爆款帖才有效
batcher 只救爆款；里程碑对所有帖普适
里程碑只对新帖有效
两者效果完全等价
why: batcher 的收益取决于窗口内事件密度（爆款专属）；里程碑与密度无关，任何帖子的写入次数都变成对数级，是更普适的一招。
why_en: Batching only helps posts with dense like bursts, whereas milestone updates cut every post's writes to a logarithmic count regardless of virality.
options_en: Both only help a handful of high-density viral posts.
Batching only helps viral posts; milestones help every post universally.
Milestones only help new posts.
They're exactly equivalent.
tradeoff: batcher 依赖点赞密度(爆款) vs 里程碑与密度无关(普适)

rows: 窗口内密集点赞的爆款

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间窗口内聚合同一帖的点赞，再一次性写回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batcher aggregates the likes for one post over a time window into a single write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在计数跨过阈值（如 2 的幂）时才写索引，把写入降为对数级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Milestone updates only write when a count crosses thresholds like powers of two.

optionExplanations: 里程碑不依赖点赞密度，对稀疏点赞的普通帖同样有效。
batcher 收益看窗口内事件密度，只帮爆款；里程碑跟密度无关，所有帖写入都降到对数级。
里程碑按点赞数打点，跟帖子新旧无关，老帖同样适用。
两者生效范围截然不同：一个挑爆款，一个覆盖全体。
optionExplanations_en: Milestones don't depend on like density, so they help sparsely-liked ordinary posts too.
Batching's payoff hinges on event density in the window, helping only viral posts; milestones are density-independent and cut every post's writes to logarithmic.
Milestones fire based on like count, unrelated to how new a post is — old posts benefit just the same.
Their reach is completely different: one targets viral posts, the other covers every post.
scenario: 点赞 100k/s 压垮 sorted set 更新，你要在 batcher 与里程碑更新之间选一个普适的减写手段。
scenario_en: Likes at 100K per second overwhelm sorted-set updates, so you pick between a batcher and milestone updates as your general write-reduction lever.

q: 交集法与 bigram 索引处理短语查询，核心权衡的维度是？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between intersection and bigram indexing for phrase queries?
options: 正确性 vs 可用性
查询计算成本 vs 索引存储成本
分布式系统的一致性 vs 分区容忍性
两者没有实质区别
why: 交集法零索引膨胀但每次查询付「传输 + 求交」的读成本；bigram 把成本预付在索引体积上，换取读时一击命中——读写成本搬运的经典权衡。
why_en: Intersection pays at query time with expensive transfers and set operations, while bigrams pay upfront with a much larger index for instant phrase lookups.
options_en: Correctness vs availability.
Query compute cost vs index storage cost.
Distributed-system consistency vs partition tolerance.
No real difference.
tradeoff: 交集法读时贵 vs bigram 存储贵

termDefinitions.meaning: 把相邻两个词组成的 token，Lucene 里叫 shingle，用于短语查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bigram (Lucene calls it a shingle) is a token made of two adjacent words.

optionExplanations: 两种方案给出的结果都正确，可用性也不是这里的分歧点。
交集法把成本留到查询时的传输和求交；bigram 把成本预付进索引体积，换查询一击命中。
这是单机数据结构的选型问题，跟分布式系统的 CAP 权衡不沾边。
两者在读时开销和索引体积上的差异非常真实，不是无差别的选择。
optionExplanations_en: Both approaches return correct results, and availability isn't the axis in play here either.
Intersection defers cost to query time — transfer and set operations; bigrams prepay that cost as a bigger index for an instant hit.
This is a single-node data-structure choice, unrelated to the CAP tradeoff in distributed systems.
The gap between read-time cost and index size is real and substantial, not an inconsequential choice.
scenario: 短语查询要么查询时求交、要么预先建 bigram 索引；存储预算和 500ms 延迟预算都很紧。
scenario_en: Phrase queries either intersect at query time or precompute a bigram index, and both the storage budget and the 500ms latency budget are tight.

q: 对这个你自己清楚的过度简化，正确的沟通动作是？
q_en: What's the right way to handle this over-simplification you know about?
options: 保持沉默，等面试官自己发现再解释
主动声明这是过度简化、稍后回来解决
当场停下，把摄取层拆成两个服务做完
只在图上标注，但口头不提及
why: 面试官会主动挑刺，未声明的缺陷会被默认为你没看见；主动认领并承诺回填，既保住推进速度又证明你看到了问题。代价是欠下一个必须兑现的 TODO。
why_en: Interviewers hunt for flaws, and an unacknowledged one is assumed to be one you missed; saying it out loud keeps your momentum while proving you saw it.
options_en: Stay silent and explain only if the interviewer notices.
Proactively flag it as over-simplified and promise to revisit.
Stop now and split ingestion into two services.
Annotate the diagram but never say it aloud.
optionExplanations: 沉默会被解读为你没看出这个规模失衡，越晚暴露越糟。
认领缺陷加承诺稍后解决，既不打断推进又展示了判断力。
当场展开会掉进兔子洞，牺牲了高层设计要求的推进速度。
面试官不一定读你的注释，口头不提等同于没声明。
optionExplanations_en: Silence reads as you missing the scale imbalance; the later it surfaces, the worse.
Owning the flaw and promising a fix keeps momentum and shows judgment.
Stopping to build it now rabbit-holes and sacrifices high-level-design pace.
The interviewer may not read your note; not saying it aloud is not flagging it.
scenario: 点赞每秒约 100k、发帖约 10k，规模差一个量级；你为快速推进先用单一摄取服务，而面试官正逐处审你的设计找缺陷。
scenario_en: Likes run ~100k/s versus ~10k/s posts, an order-of-magnitude gap, yet you use one ingestion service to move fast while the interviewer scans your design for flaws.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收发帖/点赞事件、拆词并写入倒排索引的服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ingestion service receives post and like events, tokenizes them and writes to the inverted indexes.

q: 相比简单的批处理窗口，落地里程碑方案多付出的主要代价是？
q_en: Versus a simple batching window, what is milestone counting's main added cost?
options: 索引占用的存储直接翻倍
实现复杂度和工程投入明显更高
结果排序变得不可用
对普通(非爆款)帖子完全失效
why: 里程碑要维护「下一个触发阈值」、判断是否跨越、还要把计数语义改成 approxLikes，比「30 秒窗口累加」多不少代码；换来的是写入随赞数对数增长。
why_en: Milestone logic must track the next threshold and detect crossings, far more code than a 30-second window, buying writes that grow only logarithmically with likes.
options_en: Index storage doubles outright.
Higher implementation complexity and engineering effort.
Result ordering becomes unusable.
It stops working for ordinary (non-viral) posts.
optionExplanations: 存储翻倍是「创建+点赞双索引」的代价，不是里程碑计数带来的。
维护阈值、判断跨越、改计数语义，都比窗口累加复杂得多。
排序仍近似正确，量级差距还在，并没有不可用。
失效于普通帖的是批处理窗口，里程碑对各类帖都能压缩写入。
optionExplanations_en: Doubled storage is the cost of the dual creation+likes index, not of milestones.
Tracking thresholds, detecting crossings and changing semantics all beat a window in complexity.
Ordering stays approximately correct; the magnitude gap holds, so it's not unusable.
It is the batching window that fails on ordinary posts; milestones cut writes for all posts.
scenario: 点赞索引改用里程碑计数：只在赞数跨过 2 的幂(1,2,4,8…)时才写一次，把 1000 次写压到约 10 次。
scenario_en: The likes index switches to milestone counting: it writes only when a count crosses a power of two (1,2,4,8…), turning 1000 writes into about 10.

termDefinitions.meaning: 里程碑计数下索引里的近似赞数字段，明确告知开发者它并非精确实时值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: approxLikes is the milestone-based approximate like-count field, signalling to developers that it is not exact or live.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把某帖一段时间(如 30 秒)内的点赞聚合成一次写入的方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batching window aggregates a post's likes over a fixed period (e.g. 30s) into a single write.

q: 作为 Senior，剩余时间的重心应该放在？
q_en: As a senior candidate, where should the rest of your time go?
options: 继续补更多功能需求，追求最大广度
深入优化关键路径，把取舍讲透
主动走完多个深挖并给面试官带来新认知
反复打磨 API 和数据模型的细节
why: 面试官对 Senior 期望约 40% 深度：快速过完高层设计，把时间花在关键路径优化；底线是双路径、正确倒排、合理缓存都在。
why_en: For a senior, interviewers expect ~40% depth: speed through the high-level design and spend the time optimizing the critical paths.
options_en: Keep adding more functional requirements for maximum breadth.
Go deep on the critical paths and articulate the tradeoffs.
Proactively finish several deep dives and teach the interviewer something new.
Keep polishing the API and data-model details.
optionExplanations: 一味追求广度是 Mid 级打法，Senior 要拿出深度。
关键路径(写放大、缓存、点赞索引)讲透取舍，正好对上 40% 深度的期望。
主动走完多个深挖并带来新认知是 Staff+ 的 bar，Senior 不做到也行。
API 和数据模型是基础，反复打磨挤占了关键路径优化的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Chasing breadth is a mid-level move; a senior is expected to bring depth.
Nailing the critical-path tradeoffs (write amplification, cache, likes index) matches the ~40% depth bar.
Finishing several deep dives and teaching the interviewer is the staff+ bar, not required of a senior.
The API and data model are basics; polishing them eats the time meant for critical-path work.
scenario: 你是 Senior 候选人做 FB 帖子搜索，面试官期望约 40% 深度；你已快速画完含倒排索引的可用高层设计。
scenario_en: You are a senior candidate on FB post search; the interviewer expects ~40% depth, and you have quickly drawn a working high-level design with an inverted index.
whenOtherWins: 若你是 Staff+ 候选人，仅把关键路径讲透还不够——面试官期望约 60% 深度，要主动走完多个深挖并给面试官带来新认知。
tradeoff: Senior 讲透关键路径(40%深度) vs Staff+ 多个深挖+新认知(60%深度)

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定系统性能与正确性的主链路，本题指摄取写放大、缓存、点赞索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The critical path is the chain that governs performance and correctness — here ingestion write amplification, caching and the likes index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把关键词映射到包含它的帖子 ID 列表的索引，是本题搜索的核心结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs containing it — the core search structure here.

q: 什么最能体现 Staff+ 的水准？
q_en: What best signals a staff+ level performance?
options: 把 API 和数据模型这些基础讲得格外细致
高层设计一带而过，主动多走几个深挖
严格覆盖全部功能需求的广度
画完高层设计后深入优化一条关键路径
why: 面试官已默认 Staff+ 懂 REST、数据规范化等基础，期望约 60% 深度：主动走完多个深挖，并让面试官带走新认知。
why_en: Interviewers already assume a staff+ knows the basics, so they expect ~60% depth: proactively work through several deep dives and leave them with new insight.
options_en: Explain the API and data-model basics in unusually fine detail.
Breeze through the high-level design and proactively take on several deep dives.
Rigorously cover the breadth of every functional requirement.
Draw the high-level design, then deeply optimize one critical path.
optionExplanations: 基础(REST、规范化)面试官已默认你会，细讲反而浪费宝贵的深度时间。
略过基础、主动多走深挖，正是 60% 深度并带来新认知的体现。
只顾广度是 Mid 打法，缺了 Staff+ 要的深度和主动性。
深入一条关键路径是 Senior 的 bar，Staff+ 要走完多个深挖。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer already assumes you know the basics (REST, normalization); detailing them wastes depth time.
Skipping basics and driving several deep dives is exactly the ~60% depth with new insight.
Breadth-only is a mid-level move, missing the depth and proactivity a staff+ needs.
Going deep on one critical path is the senior bar; a staff+ works through several deep dives.
scenario: 你是 Staff+ 候选人做同一道题，面试官期望约 60% 深度，且已知你懂 REST、数据规范化等基础。
scenario_en: You are a staff+ candidate on the same question; the interviewer expects ~60% depth and already assumes you know REST, data normalization and other basics.
whenOtherWins: 若你是 Senior 候选人，深入一条关键路径就够了——面试官只期望约 40% 深度，不要求走完多个深挖或带来新认知。
tradeoff: Staff+ 多个深挖+带来新认知 vs Senior 讲透一条关键路径

termDefinitions.meaning: REST(表述性状态转移)：一种基于 HTTP 动词和资源 URL 的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an API style built on HTTP verbs and resource URLs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个瓶颈或子系统的深入优化讨论，如写放大、缓存、冷存储分层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is an in-depth optimization discussion of one bottleneck or subsystem, such as write amplification, caching or cold-storage tiering.
